name: Rati Bakradze
medium: Acrylic and oil on canvas, flat opaque colour laid with a loose brush, scratchy lines drawn into the wet paint
colour: bright flat colour fields — sky blue, pink, coral red, mustard yellow, grass green and soft grey — with black shapes and small red accents
form: simple, childlike figures and animals — black dogs, horses, a bull, birds — in wide landscapes of flat bands of colour; people with oversized hands and faces, flowers and clouds as blobs; sometimes crowded scenes of many small figures
never: never photographic, never fine detail or shading, never printed text, letters or numbers, never signatures
mood: warm, humorous and a little melancholic
consent: VERBAL agreement — the owner, 2026-09-29 (his standing word: an artist he asks me to add has agreed verbally). A short written agreement (share, credit, withdrawal) is still to be signed before any label is sold.
bio: Rati Bakradze is a Georgian painter. His canvases tell small, funny and tender stories in bold, flat colour — black dogs chasing red balls, horses under huge flowers, people with oversized hands under wide skies — painted with a deliberately childlike, loose hand that turns everyday moments into quiet fables. (Draft biography — to be completed with the artist.)
